title: Breakfast map and world outline
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y5 lesson 16 (Breakfast map and world outline (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 16: Where does our food come from?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Draw an arrow from each country to the UK.

blocks.title: Sort into: Grown in the UK / Usually imported
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Grown in the UK, Usually imported.
blocks.answer: Grown in the UK: potatoes; apples; milk. Usually imported: bananas; rice; dates

keywords.def: bring goods into a country from abroad
send goods out to another country
the usual weather of a place over many years
grown at a certain time of year
food that is grown, like fruit and vegetables

questions.q: Is rice grown in the UK or imported?
Name two foods grown in the UK.

questions.a: Bring goods into a country from abroad

questions.q: Core: Make a breakfast map: list six foods from a breakfast, write where each comes from (UK or the country on the label), and mark them on the world map.
questions.a: Six foods with sensible origins marked on the map

questions.q: Extend: Write two reasons the UK imports food.
questions.a: Climate is too cool; foods out of season; cheaper abroad

questions.q: Stretch: What could happen if imports stopped?
questions.a: Some foods would disappear or cost more; we would eat more seasonal UK food

questions.q: Why are bananas imported to the UK?
questions.a: A) UK climate is too cool. Bananas need a hot, wet climate, so the UK imports them.

questions.q: Food brought into the UK from abroad is:
Big question: how many countries made your breakfast?
